# E2E — generated by QACluster

BDD framework: **features (Gherkin) → step definitions → pages**, on Playwright + TypeScript with
[playwright-bdd](https://github.com/vitalets/playwright-bdd). Generated from the code (scenarios designed by TestGraph)
and stabilized by running it against the app. **It runs on its own: no QACluster or Claude needed.**

## Structure
```
e2e/
  src/main/                              # framework code
    pages/                               # Page Objects (locators + business intentions)
    endpoints/                           # API calls used only to prepare/clean up phases already validated by UI (see below)
    entities/                            # request builders + response types for endpoints/
    fixtures/index.ts                    # DI: Pages, endpoints + ScenarioContext as scenario-scoped fixtures; exports Given/When/Then
    support/ScenarioContext.ts           # state shared between steps of ONE scenario + cleanups
    data/generators.ts                   # dynamic data: unique names/ids, relative dates
    utils/                               # generic helpers
    reporters/summary-reporter.ts        # per-run summary
  src/test/                              # what is tested
    resources/features/<flow>/<flow>.feature   # Gherkin from TestGraph — one Scenario per case: "TC-… <title>", tags @P1 @<flow> @tg-<id>
    steps/<flow>.steps.ts                # step definitions: thin, call pages; no assertions hidden in pages
    steps/common.steps.ts                # steps of no part of the app (navigation, generic checks)
    hooks/known-bugs.hooks.ts            # Before/After hooks (not glue): skips @intermittent known bugs in the normal run
    hooks/cleanup.hooks.ts               # After: undoes what the scenario created (last first)
    setup/auth.setup.ts                  # login once (storageState), if the app has login
  .features-gen/                         # generated by `bddgen` (git-ignored)
```
Imports use the aliases in `tsconfig.json` (`@fixtures`, `@pages/*`, `@support/*`, `@data/*`, `@utils/*`, `@endpoints/*`, `@entities/*`), not relative paths.

## Dependency injection (PicoContainer-style)
- A step asks for what it needs by name: `When('I save my alias', async ({ profilePage, ctx }) => …)`. It never does `new ProfilePage(page)`.
- Every fixture is **scenario-scoped**: created on first use, the **same instance** for every step of that scenario
  (across step files), and discarded at the end. `ctx` (`ScenarioContext`) is how steps share data.
- Nothing is shared between scenarios (no module-level variables, no statics, no singletons; one browser context per
  scenario). Every scenario runs **in parallel** (`fullyParallel: true`): a scenario that cleans before creating deletes
  only what earlier executions left behind more than an hour ago, never what another scenario has just created.
- New Page Object → add it to `src/main/fixtures/index.ts` once; every step can then inject it.

## UI first, API only for what is already covered
These are end-to-end tests: every step goes through the UI. A step that only **prepares** data (or **cleans it up**) may use
the API when another scenario of this suite validates that same phase through the UI — it says which one with
`// api: uiCoveredBy TC-…` (cleanups: `{ via: 'api', uiCoveredBy: 'TC-…' }`). That scenario keeps doing it through the UI.
What a case tests — its action and its assertions — is always UI. If the covering scenario is removed or becomes
`@intermittent`, `scripts/conventions-check` fails and the step must go back to the UI. API calls of a scenario are attached
to its report as `api-calls.json`. Set `API_BASE_URL` / `API_TOKEN` in `.env` (never production).

## Run
```bash
cd e2e
npm ci                           # or pnpm/yarn, depending on the repo
npx playwright install chromium
cp .env.example .env             # BASE_URL and QA credentials
npm test                         # bddgen + playwright test (parallel)
npx bddgen && npx playwright test --grep @P1      # priority 1 · --grep @smoke · --grep @regression · --grep @<flow>
qa-cluster test --tag @regression                 # from the app root: runs a tag and records the result (report + TestGraph run)
qa-cluster test --plan "Regression"               # from the app root: the automated tests of a TestGraph test plan, as a new run of it
qa-cluster test --since main                      # from the app root: the tests of the test cases that touch the code changed since a ref (or `last`)
npx bddgen && npx playwright test --workers=4     # parallelism
npm run steps                    # list every available step
npx playwright show-report       # HTML report · cucumber-report/index.html for the Gherkin view
```

## Reports of each run
| File | What for |
|---|---|
| `playwright-report/index.html` | Full report with traces, screenshots and video of failures |
| `cucumber-report/index.html` | Business-readable view: features, scenarios and steps |
| `test-results/junit.xml` | The CI's test view |
| `test-results/summary.md` / `.json` | Summary: passed, failed, flaky, known bugs (also in the GitHub job summary) |

## CI
The workflow `.github/workflows/qa-cluster-e2e.yml` (at the git root) runs this suite on PRs and on pushes to the branches it
lists. To turn it on:
1. Commit **only** the framework: `e2e/`, the workflow, `qa-cluster.config.json` and the `.gitignore` / ESLint lines the setup
   added. Do not mix in other app changes. `git diff --cached --stat` before committing.
2. Repository secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Repository secrets): every `secrets.X` the workflow
   reads — the test users and, when the backend is a private repository, `BACKEND_TOKEN` (a token with read access to it).
3. Push to a listed branch (e.g. `qa/e2e-ci`) or open a PR. The *Run workflow* button only appears once the file is on the
   default branch.
4. CI tests the **committed** code. If QACluster ran on uncommitted changes, CI may fail where the local run passed.
5. Results: the case table is on the run's **Summary** page; the full reports are in the `e2e-report-<id>` artifact (also
   when the run fails or times out), with `test-results/runner-resources.txt` (memory, processes the kernel killed).
6. Public HTML report (only when the workflow has the `publish-report` job): in the repo, **Settings → Pages → Source =
   GitHub Actions**, and **Settings → Environments → github-pages → Deployment branches**: add every branch that runs the
   workflow (by default only `main` may publish). The site shows the last run; anyone with the link sees it, screenshots
   and videos included.

## Known bugs
Scenarios tagged `@fail @BUG-NNN` reproduce confirmed product bugs (see the QACluster report): the suite stays green and the
bug stays visible. If one passes, the run is green and the summary says the bug is **fixed**: `qa-cluster test --tag <tag>`
removes both tags and closes the bug when it runs that scenario; by hand, remove the tags and the bug's entry in
`.qa-cluster/known-bugs.json`.

Scenarios tagged `@intermittent @BUG-NNN` reproduce product bugs that only show up some of the time. They are skipped in
`npm test` (summary: *known intermittent*) so they never turn CI red at random. `npm run test:intermittent` runs only them,
4 times each, and the summary shows the failure rate per bug (it exits non-zero while the bug reproduces; run it as a
non-blocking job). 0 failures out of 4 → **bug fixed?**: verify it and remove both tags. A bug that shows up very rarely
can pass 4 runs: verify by hand before removing the tags (or raise `--repeat-each` in the script).

A failure that matches a known bug **not** tagged on that scenario (`e2e/.qa-cluster/known-bugs.json`, often a suspected
bug in a setup step) stays a failure, but the summary names it: *matches BUG-NNN (suspected) in the precondition*. The case
never reached what it verifies: fix or track that bug, not the test.

## Maintenance
- `.qa-cluster.json` records what QACluster generated; files edited by people are not overwritten on the next run.
- Feature files mirror TestGraph scenarios (exported as Gherkin from the dashboard). Change the behavior in TestGraph, not only here.

## Run locally (this repo)

`npm test` starts the app itself through `webServer` (these commands), and reuses it when it is already running:
```
python3 -m http.server 4180 --bind 127.0.0.1
```
